issues.title: Viewport dimensions drift after full-page screenshot

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
1. resize 1280 900
2. goto any URL
3. screenshot (verify: 1600×1125 physical / 1280×900 CSS)
4. screenshot --full-page
5. scroll up 5000
6. screenshot
7. eval 'window.innerWidth' → 1728 not 1280

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Viewport should remain at 1280×900 CSS pixels after full-page screenshot.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Viewport grew from 1280×900 (1600×1125 physical at 1.25 DPR) to 1728×1034 (2160×1292 physical). The resize command's effect was silently undone or mutated by a subsequent operation — likely the full-page screenshot temporarily adjusting the viewport and failing to restore it.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The full-page screenshot likely uses CDP to temporarily set the viewport height to the full page height (or uses Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride) and fails to restore the original dimensions afterward. The resize command may also set the outer window size rather than the inner content area, leading to confusion about what '1280×900' actually means.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-browser/ — PulsarWebDriver screenshot/fullPage logic or the CDP Page.captureScreenshot invocation that temporarily resizes the viewport.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- After full-page screenshot, restore the original viewport dimensions explicitly via CDP
- Consider using `Page.captureScreenshot` with `captureBeyondViewport: true` instead of resizing the viewport
- Add a `--viewport` flag to `resize` that distinguishes between CSS pixels and device pixels
- Verify and report actual viewport dimensions after resize (e.g., "Resized to 1280×900 (inner: 1280×900, DPR: 1.25)")

issues.title: Full-page screenshot saves as JPEG despite .png extension

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
1. goto any URL
2. screenshot --full-page --filename output.png
3. file output.png → "JPEG image data" despite .png extension

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: File extension should match the actual image format, or the format should be documented.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The file has a `.png` extension but contains JPEG data. This is misleading — tools that check magic bytes will correctly identify it as JPEG, but users and scripts relying on the extension will be confused.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Likely the full-page screenshot path uses CDP's `Page.captureScreenshot` which returns JPEG by default for large screenshots (smaller file size), but the CLI always appends `.png` to the filename regardless of the actual format.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — screenshot command handler that determines the output filename extension.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Detect the actual image format from the CDP response and use the correct extension (.jpg for JPEG, .png for PNG)
- Or force PNG format for consistency with the extension
- Or allow a `--format png|jpeg` flag so users can choose

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
1. Run `b4w.ps1 help`
2. Read the filter line: "Filter help by category: --help nav | --help extract | --help session | --help kb | --help agent | --help swarm | --help crawl"
3. Try `--help capture`, `--help mouse`, `--help core`, `--help kb` — all work but aren't listed

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: All valid help category filters should be listed in the main help output.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The main help only advertises 7 filter categories (nav, extract, session, kb, agent, swarm, crawl) but `capture`, `mouse`, and `core` also work. The Global options section also lists a subset: "try: nav, extract, session, kb, agent".

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The help category filter list in the CLI's help text is hardcoded and was not updated when new categories (capture, mouse, core) were added. Two different lists exist (the Filter line at top and the Global options hint at bottom) with different contents.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — help text generation, likely in main.rs or a help module.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Generate the category filter list dynamically from registered categories instead of hardcoding
- Unify the two lists (filter line and Global options hint) to avoid inconsistency
- Add `capture`, `mouse`, and `core` to the advertised categories

issues.title: No 'scroll to top' or 'scroll to bottom' convenience command

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
1. scroll down 3000
2. Try to scroll back to top — must guess pixel amount (scroll up 3000) or use eval with window.scrollTo()

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A shorthand command like `scroll top` or `scroll bottom` so users don't have to track how far they've scrolled.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Only pixel-based relative scrolling is available via `scroll <direction> <pixels>`. Users must remember or guess how far they scrolled down to get back to the top.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The scroll command only supports relative pixel offsets. Positional targets (top, bottom) were not implemented.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — scroll command implementation.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Support `scroll top` and `scroll bottom` as aliases that scroll to position 0 and document height respectively
- Consider `scroll to <pixels>` for absolute positioning as a complement to the relative `scroll <direction> <pixels>`

issues.title: Wait command output lacks context about what was waited for

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
1. wait --load networkidle
2. Output: "✓ Wait complete" — no indication of what condition was satisfied or how long it took.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Output should include the condition that was satisfied, e.g., "✓ Network idle reached (took 1.2s)" or "✓ Text 'Training' found on page".

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Uniform "✓ Wait complete" for all wait modes. Users can't tell from the output whether anything actually happened or the condition was already met.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The wait command uses a generic success message regardless of the wait mode, discarding mode-specific context that would help users understand what happened.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — wait command output formatting.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Include the wait mode in the output: "✓ Network idle reached", "✓ Text 'X' found", "✓ Element 'e1' appeared"
- Include elapsed time: "(took 1.2s)" or "(already satisfied)"
- Distinguish between "waited and found" vs "already satisfied" for debuggability

issues.title: Resize command unclear about outer window vs inner viewport

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
1. resize 1280 900 → "✓ Resized to 1280×900"
2. eval 'window.innerWidth' → 1728 (not 1280)
3. Confusion: what does 1280×900 actually control?

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The command should clarify whether it resizes the outer browser window, the inner content area (viewport), and whether device pixel ratio affects the result. Output should report the actual resulting viewport dimensions.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The output says "1280×900" but the actual viewport CSS dimensions are different (1728×1034 in testing). The relationship between the requested size and the actual viewport is opaque to the user.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The resize command likely sets the outer window size via CDP `Browser.setWindowBounds`, but the inner content area is smaller due to browser chrome (title bar, toolbars). The device pixel ratio also affects physical vs CSS pixel dimensions. None of this is explained.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-browser/ — PulsarWebDriver resize logic.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Report both requested and actual viewport dimensions: "Resized window to 1280×900 (viewport: 1280×858, DPR: 1.25)"
- Document the distinction between outer window size and inner viewport in `resize --help`
- Consider adding a `--viewport` flag that targets the inner content area directly via CDP Emulation

issues.title: Default screenshot save location is not obvious to first-time users

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
1. screenshot (no --filename)
2. Output shows path under .browser4-cli/snapshot/ with timestamp filename
3. User may not know where .browser4-cli/ lives or how to find the file later

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The output should make it easy to locate and use the file, perhaps with a relative path from CWD or a copyable command.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Output shows an absolute path which is helpful, but the directory `.browser4-cli/` is a hidden directory (dot-prefixed) that new users might not know about. The clickable link format in the terminal is good though.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Design choice to store artifacts in `.browser4-cli/snapshot/`. This is fine for power users but could be surfaced more clearly for newcomers.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a tip after the first screenshot: "Screenshots are saved to .browser4-cli/snapshot/. Use --filename to choose a custom location."
- Consider `screenshot --open` to open the file in the system viewer
- List recent screenshots in the session summary
